
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

# Image paths for the four pieces split out of the original infographic
imgs <- c(
  scenario1      = "images/scenario1.png",
  scenario2      = "images/scenario2.png",
  scenario3      = "images/scenario3.png",
  transformation = "images/transformation.png"
)

# Helper: wrap one image in a reveal.js fragment <div>, so it is revealed
# incrementally (one click = one fragment appears), in DOM order.
fragment_cell <- function(path, css_class) {
  sprintf(
    '<div class="fragment %s"><img src="%s"></div>',
    css_class, path
  )
}

# Row 1: three columns, one scenario image each (fragments 1, 2, 3)
row1 <- paste0(
  "<tr>",
  "<td>", fragment_cell(imgs[["scenario1"]], "scenario-img"), "</td>",
  "<td>", fragment_cell(imgs[["scenario2"]], "scenario-img"), "</td>",
  "<td>", fragment_cell(imgs[["scenario3"]], "scenario-img"), "</td>",
  "</tr>"
)

# Row 2: one column spanning all three, the transformation image
# (fragment 4 - always the last fragment on the slide)
row2 <- paste0(
  "<tr>",
  '<td colspan="3" class="transform-cell">',
  fragment_cell(imgs[["transformation"]], "transform-img"),
  "</td>",
  "</tr>"
)

html_table <- paste0(
  '<table class="journey-table">',
  row1,
  row2,
  "</table>"
)

cat(html_table)
```
